answers.text: Have the assistant always give three lines in the same order: drop-off time, then pallet count, then any damage noted, with just that info on each line.
List the customer, topic and outcome for each call that still needs a follow-up.
Something seems a little quick about the schedule in this note, might be worth a second look before it's filed.
I checked the on-time rate, 9 late out of 118, and that lines up with the 92% they wrote.
I'd go with the second one, it shows the ticket numbers.

I'd send the second email, it has the actual volume numbers, 1,200 up to 1,650, to back up the ask. The first one just says 'better rate' without saying by how much our volume grew, so there's nothing to point to if they push back.
1. Careful with the pricing there. 2. Yes. 3. Should be okay, it's not signed off yet but it's just a draft. 4. Not sure, maybe not. 5. No.
The hourly rates in the agreement I'd be cautious about pasting in.
Before the monthly stock summary goes to my manager, I'd check the counted total against what's in the system.
The first step, reading the invoice PDF, is the one I'd watch since mistakes there carry through.
